indian.headline: Indian markets closed mixed as banking gains offset IT weakness; crude oil retreat supported sentiment.
indian.lead: Indian markets closed mixed as banking gains offset IT weakness; crude oil retreat supported sentiment.
indian.brief: Sensex fell 0.24% and Nifty 50 dropped 0.52%, while Bank Nifty rose 0.47% on a day of mixed sector moves.
indian.narrative:
Markets opened weak after US sanctions on Iran spooked traders, but recovered as crude oil prices fell over 6% in two sessions to around $80, easing inflation concerns. Banking stocks outperformed with a +0.5% gain, supported by crude retreat and what traders called a new auction window swing. However, IT shares dragged with a -1.5% decline, while pharma held steady at +0.2%.

On the corporate front, L&T grabbed headlines winning two mega West Asia contracts worth ₹20,000–₹25,000 crore, lifting shares 0.71%. HEG announced a September 7 record date for its demerger into graphite electrodes and a separate entity. boAt posted strong FY26 results with 38% profit growth to ₹84.5 crore, driven by wearables. Meanwhile, Kirloskar Brothers shares slipped 1.2% after the Supreme Court ordered a family dispute to arbitration, creating near-term uncertainty.

tiles.label: Global cues
tiles.sub: US Iran sanctions initially weighed; crude retreat and easing global yields offset early weakness.

tiles.label: FII activity
tiles.sub: No fresh data on foreign flows reported today.

tiles.label: Crude oil
tiles.sub: Down over 6% in two sessions to ~₹80, easing inflation worries and supporting sentiment.

indian.watch: Monitor crude oil trends and US geopolitical moves; watch HEG demerger execution and L&T contract progress.

us.headline: US markets close higher on tech strength; energy sector struggles amid mixed economic signals.
us.lead: US markets close higher on tech strength; energy sector struggles amid mixed economic signals.
us.brief: S&P 500 gained 0.32%, Nasdaq rose 0.66%, and Dow added 0.30%, with tech leading at +0.9% while energy fell 1.7%.
us.narrative:
US equities finished Tuesday in the green, driven by solid performance in technology and healthcare stocks. The Nasdaq outpaced broader indices, reflecting investor appetite for growth names. Energy stocks bucked the trend, posting the day's only significant loss, possibly signaling caution over global demand concerns.

Corporate news painted a mixed picture. United Airlines announced expansion into premium leisure routes while grappling with delayed Boeing aircraft decisions. Dick's Sporting Goods' weak earnings pressured the footwear sector, and trade tensions escalated as Trump threatened to raise Canadian auto tariffs from 25% to 50% starting January. Tesla faced its largest Chinese vehicle recall over safety concerns, adding pressure to the auto sector's outlook.

tiles.label: Big mover
tiles.sub: Nasdaq led indices; healthcare also positive at +0.3%.

tiles.label: Key data
tiles.sub: Sector weakness despite broader market gains; demand concerns evident.

tiles.label: Backdrop
tiles.sub: Growth optimism offset by trade war escalation and corporate headwinds.

us.watch: Monitor US-Canada trade negotiations and Tesla's response to China recall; tariff moves could reshape auto valuations.
